references.text: Moses chose seventy elders in Israel who received a share of the Spirit to help him—a possible foreshadowing of Jesus' selection of the seventy (two).

The Lord asked Moses to come up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders. The number seventy is linked to leadership in Israel and may lie behind Jesus' choice of seventy (two) emissaries.
The genealogies in Genesis 10 mention seventy (or seventy-two) nations, which may point to the sending out of the seventy-two as a sign of the universal reach of the gospel.
Jesus sent out the twelve apostles with authority to preach and heal—an earlier parallel to the sending of the seventy-two in Luke 10.
Jesus sent out the twelve two by two, the same pattern ('ἀνὰ δύο δύο') used for the sending of the seventy-two.
Jesus sent messengers ahead of him ('πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ') to a Samaritan village to prepare his coming, a closely parallel expression to Luke 10:1.
Malachi prophesies: 'See, I am sending my messenger before me to clear the way.' The phrase 'πρὸ προσώπου' is used for forerunners sent ahead, just as the seventy-two were sent ahead of Jesus.
A voice cries out to make a way for the Lord—a prophetic foreshadowing of the idea of envoys going before the Lord to prepare his coming.
The seventy-two return with joy and report that demons submit in Jesus' name—the direct follow-up to the sending in Luke 10:1.
The Holy Spirit instructs the church to send out Barnabas and Saulus for missionary work—a continuation of the principle that the Lord sends workers out in pairs for preaching.
